blocks.raw: <WikiMistakeList mistakes={[{"mistake":"Low-cost housing is a statutory classification in BP 220.","fact":"BP 220 defines only socialized (72/28 lot, 22 floor) and economic (100 lot, 42 floor) housing. Low-cost is an industry-recognized segment between economic and open-market, but not a legal classification."},{"mistake":"Economic housing has a minimum lot area of 72 sq.m.","fact":"72 sq.m. is socialized housing (new subdivision). Economic housing is 100 sq.m. minimum lot area under BP 220."},{"mistake":"Socialized housing on-site or off-site changes its classification from socialized to something else.","fact":"On-site and off-site are delivery methods, not classifications. Both deliver socialized housing; the location and financing source do not change the legal classification."},{"mistake":"NHA is responsible for financing end-buyer housing loans.","fact":"NHA builds housing; Pag-IBIG/HDMF finances loans to individual buyers. These are distinct functions."},{"mistake":"A private developer building a luxury subdivision has no responsibility to produce affordable housing.","fact":"RA 7279 and RA 10884 require open-market developers to produce balanced housing equivleant to 15–20% of project cost as socialized units."},{"mistake":"The Community Mortgage Program (CMP) is a classification of housing.","fact":"CMP is a delivery method (SHFC financing for community land purchases) that can deliver socialized or economic housing. It is not itself a classification."}]} />
